findings.text: The _load_file_history docstring still states 'No stored read inspects per-run documents or refreshes their disposable indexes', which this change makes false: the stored branch at reckon/ledger.py:2841-2846 now scandirs the runs directory and decodes every document the store does not hold on each stored read, so the module's own contract text contradicts the behaviour it documents.

The done_when requires the arm over the ledger-importing test files to be recorded as inline JSON carrying full 40-character revisions, but baseline_suite/after_suite name tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py (0 failures in both logs), which import no ledger module; the ledger arm (6 failed 171 passed at 2437205f9a762420c943f3c0b0312ded03f7395f versus 4 failed 173 passed at 70c0ce43867b29585ae82013218a1981feb2055d) exists only as prose in artifacts beside logs/ledger-arm-base.log and logs/ledger-arm-head.log, so a promotion reading only the JSON arms sees a pair that never exercises the change.

The done_when's 'ruff check and ruff format --check report nothing new on the changed paths' clause rests on prose in the artifacts line with no log or command recorded, so no artefact lets a reader establish the claim without repeating the work.

notes: Durability is a reading, not an experiment: the diff adds no assertion, and the guard is the pre-existing named file, which reddens on the reinstated regression - at 2437205f9a762420c943f3c0b0312ded03f7395f the stored branch answers _report_damaged_run_records(project, ()) and logs/torn-ledger-base-red.log records test_review_pass_keeps_promoting_with_a_truncated_row and test_read_during_exclusive_append_reports_damage_then_recovers[True] failing on 'assert () == (PosixPath(...),)'. Those expectations are independent of the value under test: the expected tuple holds a path the test itself wrote and the actual value comes from ledger.damaged_run_records, so restoring the empty-tuple call reddens them. The nine-file arm's head failing ids are a strict subset of the base's (verified from logs/ledger-arm-base.log and logs/ledger-arm-head.log), the four remainder matching the manifest's outside_scope. Reuse search: grep over reckon/ for damaged_run_records, for an enumerator of unheld run documents, and for the run-directory listing owners (_run_files at reckon/ledger.py:1054, _run_files_written_since at :2940, _merge_run_documents at :2976) found no owner for reporting damage among documents the store does not hold; the new helper calls the existing _read_run, ledger_path and _report_damaged_run_records rather than adding a second damage rule or a parallel damaged set.
